body.translated_text: Homage to the Protector of the World (<s>Lokanātha</s>)!

children.translated_text: One should first firmly generate <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening), born of the power of compassion (<s>kāruṇya</s>),
unattached to the pleasures of worldly existence, turning away from possessions.
Endowed with the wealth of faith and the other [virtues], one should serve the <s>guru</s> as equal to the <s>Buddha</s>,
striving to observe the conduct and commitments (<s>samaya</s>) taught by him.
Through the guru's grace, one receives the <s>kumbha</s> (vase), <s>guhya</s> (secret), and [other] <s>abhiṣekas</s> (initiations);
purified in body, speech, and mind, that practitioner (<s>sādhaka</s>) becomes a vessel for <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment).
Filled with the accumulations (<s>saṃbhāra</s>) that arise from the limbs of <s>samādhi</s> (meditation),
accomplishment is swiftly attained — such is the established way of the secret <s>mantra</s> (<s>guhyamantra</s>).
When there is a falling away from the limbs of <s>samādhi</s>, and likewise when the opposing factors are established,
<s>samādhi</s> will not be accomplished even in thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of lifetimes.
Therefore, the <s>yogin</s> established in the secret practice, for the purpose of accomplishing that <s>samādhi</s>,

children.text: tad bhinnaṃ cintanaṃ tyaktvā dṛḍhavīryeṇa codyamet // 6 //
children.translated_text: should abandon thinking that is contrary to it and strive with firm vigor.
The limbs of <s>samādhi</s> and the opposing factors, in their determination —
the limbs of <s>samādhi</s> and the opposing factors are here briefly stated.
Perfection of moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>), indifference toward enjoyments,
<s>kṣānti</s> (patience), firm resolve, and avoidance of company with [worldly] people,
clear comprehension (<s>samprajanya</s>) conjoined with the activities of body, speech, and mind,
mindfulness of the body (<s>kāyānusmṛti</s>) conjoined with recollection of the <s>Buddha's</s> form and praise,

children.text: yasmin kāle tu yatkārya dārḍhrya tasya hyanusmṛtau /
children.translated_text: firmness in recollecting what is to be done at whatever time,
abandonment of the five hindrances (<s>pañcāvaraṇa</s>), acting with propriety, devotion, and respect,
equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>) of mind always toward all worldly conditions (<s>lokadharmā</s>),
and austerity (<s>saṃlekha</s>) — these are the limbs [of <s>samādhi</s>]; the opposing factors are their opposites.

body.text: samādhisambhārakṛtairhi puṇyaiḥ samādhiṃ vajropamametu lokaḥ / 12, a ba /
body.translated_text: By the merits of having cultivated the accumulations for <s>samādhi</s>, may the world attain the <s>vajra</s>-like <s>samādhi</s>!
The <s>Samādhisaṃbhāraparivarta</s>, composed by the great <s>paṇḍita</s> and master <s>Dīpaṃkaraśrījñānapāda</s> (<s>Atiśa</s>), is completed.

body.text: tenaiva bhāratīyopādhyāyena mahāsaṃśodhakalokacakṣuṣā bhikṣu-śākyamatinā ca anūdya nirṇītaḥ //
body.translated_text: It was translated and finalized by that same Indian preceptor, the great editor and eye of the world, and the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Śākyamati</s>.
